title: Early embryo death is a frequent cause of sterility in first crosses

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Early embryo death is a frequent cause of sterility in first crosses

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: A very frequent cause of sterility in first crosses between species is the early death of the embryo, which may be exposed to unsuitable conditions within the mother or the egg or seed.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the early death of the embryo is a very frequent cause of sterility in first crosses.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VIII, “Hybridism”; section “Causes of the sterility of first crosses and of hybrids”. Scope: interspecific first crosses, especially gallinaceous birds and plants

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch08-09: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.73

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Failure stage is directly observable and many datasets document hybrid embryogenesis. Biased and incomplete taxonomic coverage prevents reliable resolution of the claimed general frequency.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Stage reciprocal interspecific crosses and classify failure as pre-fertilization, embryonic death, later mortality, or adult sterility. Estimate the fraction of first-cross infertility attributable to early embryo death.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Negative and failed crosses are underreported.

'Very frequent' requires representative sampling across taxa.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data existence: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.66
discriminating power: 0.87
operationalizability: 0.95

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The frequency of early embryo death is a clear proportion, but open compilations usually score inviability without the stage. Stage-resolved cases exist in papers on a few birds, plants, and model animals, which is enough for a partial look and not enough for the stated generality. Building the denominator would be slow literature work.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Among first crosses that fail, record the fraction in which fertilization occurs and the embryo dies early, versus no fertilization or death at a later stage. A large share of early embryonic death would support 'very frequent'; a minority share would refute that wording.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Crosses that produce no visible embryo are easily misclassified.

Most isolation indices do not record the developmental stage of death.

Gallinaceous birds and plants, the groups Darwin emphasized, lack a public stage-of-failure table.
